changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: Send us a month of your failed renewals and we'll show you which ones would have come back with a retry or an updated card. For membership and subscription buyers, open with: 'How much of your churn is members who never meant to leave, cards that just failed?' and get their own figure before quoting any of ours.
changes.why: The recovery claim landed because it was demonstrated on the customer's own failed-renewal export, and the customer's phrase 'members who never meant to leave' describes the problem more sharply than 'smart retries'.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop leading with the global, every-currency opener for domestic multi-site buyers (here, US and Canada studios). Lead with the churn question instead: 'How much of your churn is cards that just failed?'
changes.why: The global opener drew silence from a US and Canada customer, while the board-level churn question and the failed-payment split were what started and held the evaluation.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For studio and multi-site buyers with front-desk hardware, stop claiming one platform across till and web until the studio-software reader integration can be shown live. Say plainly what runs through a partner, and answer readers, studio-software compatibility, contract term and exit cost early in the deck.
changes.why: 'Unified commerce' was heard as 'is that the readers?', the in-their-software demo could not be shown live because it depends on a partner, and phase two is still undated.

changes.change: New finance-approver line, for the controller or budget owner: 'Give us one month of your failed renewals and we'll show you, in your own numbers, what comes back, what it costs, and what it costs to leave.' Pair it with a one-page summary of own-data results, contract terms and termination fees, and run the data session before paper goes out.
changes.why: The controller who held the signature sat on the paper for two weeks, asked about termination fees twice, then asked for the spreadsheet in the data session and signed four days later.
